fight: Whether an asset-light marketplace model is structurally superior to a 1P inventory-owning model in emerging market B2B FMCG.

side_a.position: 1P model provides full operational control, guaranteed fulfillment, higher nominal gross margins, and private-label capture.
claims: 1P inventory ownership allows guaranteed OTIF and higher markup margins

side_b.position: Asset-light is the only survivable model; 1P gross margins are swallowed by logistics/warehouse costs and destroyed by currency devaluation.
claims: Asset-light model enables positive EBIT and capital resilience during funding winters

evidence_quality_delta: Empirical proof favors Side B: 1P players collapsed or faced downrounds; asset-light players reached profitability.
scope_overlap: Genuine structural conflict over capital intensity and margin economics.

fight: Whether an asset-light B2B marketplace inevitably suffers disintermediation once retailer and wholesaler discover each other.

side_a.position: Disintermediation is inevitable in low-margin FMCG; merchants bypass the platform to save 2% commission.
claims: Wholesalers and retailers bypass platforms when commissions are introduced

side_b.position: Disintermediation is prevented when the platform bundles multi-vendor carts, bank credit lines, and wholesaler ERP software.
claims: Multi-vendor basket aggregation, bank credit, and wholesaler software prevent platform bypass

evidence_quality_delta: Empirical: GudangAda suffered bypass because it was free and lacked credit lock-in; OmniRetail achieved zero bypass via Mplify and OmniPay.
scope_overlap: Depends on platform value proposition depth beyond simple catalog listing.

fight: Whether B2B platforms should fund merchant working capital from their own balance sheet or strictly through banking partners.

side_a.position: Proprietary lending captures higher interest spreads and enables instant risk decisions.
claims: Direct balance sheet lending drives rapid GMV and higher finance revenue

side_b.position: Balance sheet lending in macro-volatile markets causes fatal default write-offs; data underwriting with bank partners is mandatory.
claims: Partnering with commercial banks offloads default risk while monetizing transaction telemetry

evidence_quality_delta: Empirical: Capiter and TradeDepot faced severe credit distress; VinShop/Techcombank and Cartona/AMAN scaled safely.
scope_overlap: Tripartite partnership versus balance sheet ownership.

fight: Whether B2B ordering should enforce a single-wholesaler basket or dynamically split orders across multiple vendors.

side_a.position: Single-vendor cart is necessary to avoid delivery chaos and keep transport simple.
claims: Single-vendor orders simplify last-mile logistics for store owners

side_b.position: Single-vendor causes high basket abandonment; dynamic clustered split (max 2 vendors) balances price, availability, and logistics.
claims: Clustered dynamic routing achieves high fill rates while keeping drops manageable

scope_overlap: Trade-off between SKU fill-rate and delivery drop coordination.

fight: Whether traditional FMCG retail can transition to pure digital self-serve or permanently requires visiting sales reps.

side_a.position: Traditional retail is relationship-driven; store owners will never order without a visiting rep.
claims: Sales reps are permanently required for order booking in traditional retail

side_b.position: Reps are necessary for onboarding and first 3 orders, but stores naturally transition to late-night self-serve ordering.
claims: Over 75-80% of mature store reorders migrate to autonomous digital self-serve

evidence_quality_delta: Empirical conversion tracking across 100,000+ stores in Egypt, Pakistan, and Philippines.
scope_overlap: Lifecycle progression from onboarding to habituation.
